scenes.headline: Renunciation with Self-Knowledge
visual: Who Krishna really is, and what action really is
scenes.say: Chapter Four. The Path of Renunciation with Self-Knowledge. Here Krishna reveals two secrets: who he really is, and what action really is.

scenes.verse: The Supreme Lord said: I taught this Karma-yoga, the eternal science of selfless action, to King Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu. Manu taught it to Ikshvaku. Thus handed down in succession the saintly Kings knew this. After a long time the science of Karma-yoga was lost from this earth. Today I have described the same ancient science to you because you are my sincere devotee and friend. Karma-yoga is the supreme secret indeed.
scenes.say: He begins with a surprising claim about the teaching itself. The Supreme Lord said: I taught this Karma-yoga, the eternal science of selfless action, to King Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu. Manu taught it to Ikshvaku. Thus handed down in succession the saintly Kings knew this. After a long time the science of Karma-yoga was lost from this earth. Today I have described the same ancient science to you because you are my sincere devotee and friend. Karma-yoga is the supreme secret indeed.

scenes.headline: How can that be?
visual: Arjuna: you were born after Vivasvan
Krishna: we have both had many births
I remember them all; you do not
scenes.say: Arjuna is puzzled. You were born long after the sun-king Vivasvan, he says. How could you have taught him in the beginning? Krishna answers calmly: both you and I have taken many births. I remember them all, Arjuna. You do not. Though I am unborn and eternal, I take form through my own divine power.

scenes.verse: Whenever there is a decline of Dharma (Righteousness) and a predominance of Adharma (or Unrighteousness), O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself. I appear from time to time for protecting the good, for transforming the wicked, and for establishing world order (Dharma).
scenes.say: And then he says why. These may be the most quoted lines in India. Whenever there is a decline of Dharma (Righteousness) and a predominance of Adharma (or Unrighteousness), O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself. I appear from time to time for protecting the good, for transforming the wicked, and for establishing world order (Dharma).

scenes.headline: Every seeker is met
visual: Whoever understands this is not born again
Many reached freedom by taking refuge in Him
With whatever motive people worship, He answers
scenes.say: Whoever truly understands these divine appearances, Krishna says, is not born again. Many before Arjuna became free from attachment, fear and anger by taking refuge in him. And whatever the motive with which people come to him, he meets them there and answers them accordingly.

scenes.verse: The one who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is a wise person. Such a person is a yogi and has accomplished everything.
scenes.say: Then Krishna turns to the riddle at the heart of the chapter: what is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused about it. Verse eighteen. The one who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is a wise person. Such a person is a yogi and has accomplished everything.

scenes.verse: The one who has abandoned attachment to the fruits of work, and remains ever content and dependent on no one but God, such a person — though engaged in activity — does nothing at all and incurs no Karmic reaction, good or bad.
scenes.say: He explains what he means. Verse twenty. The one who has abandoned attachment to the fruits of work, and remains ever content and dependent on no one but God, such a person — though engaged in activity — does nothing at all and incurs no Karmic reaction, good or bad.

scenes.headline: Many kinds of offering
visual: Worship, study and sense restraint
Breath control, fasting and charity
All purify those who practise them
scenes.say: Krishna then describes many kinds of spiritual practice, each one a form of sacrifice: worship, the study of scripture, restraint of the senses, control of the breath, a simple diet, charity. All of these, done sincerely, purify the person who practises them.

scenes.verse: The acquisition and propagation of Self-knowledge are superior to any material gain or gift, O Arjuna. Because all actions in their entirety culminate in knowledge.
scenes.say: But one offering stands above the rest. Verse thirty-three. The acquisition and propagation of Self-knowledge are superior to any material gain or gift, O Arjuna. Because all actions in their entirety culminate in knowledge.

scenes.verse: Acquire this spiritual knowledge from a Self-realized guru by humble reverence, by sincere inquiry, and by service. The wise ones who have realized the Truth will teach you.
scenes.say: And where does such knowledge come from? Verse thirty-four. Acquire this spiritual knowledge from a Self-realized guru by humble reverence, by sincere inquiry, and by service. The wise ones who have realized the Truth will teach you.

scenes.verse: As the blazing fire reduces wood to ashes; similarly, the fire of Self-knowledge reduces all bonds of Karma (or sin) to ashes, O Arjuna.
scenes.say: Its power is total. Verse thirty-seven. As the blazing fire reduces wood to ashes; similarly, the fire of Self-knowledge reduces all bonds of Karma (or sin) to ashes, O Arjuna.

scenes.verse: Therefore, cut the ignorance-born doubt about the Supreme Being abiding in your mind by the sword of Self-knowledge, resort to Karma-yoga, and get up for the war, O Arjuna.
scenes.say: And the chapter ends, as so many do, with a call to rise. Verse forty-two. Therefore, cut the ignorance-born doubt about the Supreme Being abiding in your mind by the sword of Self-knowledge, resort to Karma-yoga, and get up for the war, O Arjuna.

scenes.headline: Karma-Yoga Is an Ancient, Eternal Science
visual: Taught at the beginning of creation
Passed down through saintly kings
Restored by God whenever it is lost
scenes.say: Lesson one. Karma-yoga is an ancient, eternal science. Selfless action is not a new idea Krishna invents on the battlefield. It was taught at the dawn of creation and handed down through saintly rulers, and when it is forgotten, God restores it.

scenes.headline: God Incarnates to Restore Righteousness
visual: When righteousness declines, God appears
To protect the good
To transform the wicked and restore order
scenes.say: Lesson two. God incarnates to restore righteousness. Whenever dharma declines and wrong rises, the Divine takes form, to protect the good, to transform the wicked, and to set the world right again. It is not random. It has a purpose.

scenes.headline: Understanding God's Nature Leads to Liberation
visual: Knowing God's appearances truly
Frees one from rebirth
Liberation needs understanding, not only behaviour
scenes.say: Lesson three. Understanding God's nature leads to liberation. Whoever truly understands the divine nature of God's appearances and works is freed from rebirth. Freedom is not only about good behaviour; it needs real understanding.

scenes.headline: God Fulfills Devotees According to Their Motive
visual: People seek God for many reasons
Success, knowledge, love or freedom
Each is met on their own path
scenes.say: Lesson four. God fulfils devotees according to their motive. People turn to the Divine for many reasons: success, knowledge, love, freedom. Krishna does not reject any of them. He meets each person on the path they have chosen.

scenes.headline: Karma Does Not Bind God — or Those Who Understand This
visual: God acts constantly, yet is not bound
He has no desire for the results
Whoever lives this is not bound either
scenes.say: Lesson five. Karma does not bind God, or those who understand this. God acts all the time, creating and sustaining, yet no karma touches him, because he wants nothing from the results. Anyone who understands and lives the same way is not bound either.

scenes.headline: Inaction in action, action in inaction
visual: Selfless action | Selfish inaction
Busy, yet free of ego | Idle, yet full of desire
Creates no karma | Still creates karma
Truly inaction | Truly action
scenes.say: Lesson six. Selfless action is inaction; selfish inaction is action. A person working hard without ego or desire is, in the deepest sense, not acting at all, because nothing binds them. A person sitting idle, but burning with desire, is acting all the time. What matters is the inner state, not the outer motion.

scenes.headline: A Karma-Yogi Accumulates No Karmic Debt
visual: Free from attachment and craving
Mind and senses under control
Work as service creates no karmic debt
scenes.say: Lesson seven. A Karma-yogi accumulates no karmic debt. When you are free from attachment, your mind and senses are steady, you claim no ownership of the outcome, and you work as service to God, no karma clings to you, whatever the work.

scenes.headline: Many Paths of Spiritual Practice Are Valid
visual: Worship, study, breath, charity, fasting
Practised sincerely, all are valid
There is more than one way in
scenes.say: Lesson eight. Many paths of spiritual practice are valid. Krishna lists a wide range: worship, study, restraint, breath, charity, fasting. Practised with sincerity and selflessness, every one of them purifies. There is more than one way in.

scenes.headline: Self-Knowledge Is Superior to All Other Spiritual Offerings
visual: Of all offerings, knowledge is highest
All actions culminate in knowledge
Sharing it is the greatest gift
scenes.say: Lesson nine. Self-knowledge is superior to all other spiritual offerings. Rituals, gifts and disciplines all have value, but they all point toward something. The acquisition and the sharing of self-knowledge is where every action finally leads.

scenes.headline: Seek Truth From a Self-Realized Teacher
visual: Approach a realised teacher
With humility, honest questions and service
Some knowledge can't come from books alone
scenes.say: Lesson ten. Seek truth from a self-realised teacher. Some knowledge cannot come from books alone. Approach someone who has lived it, with humility, with sincere questions, and with a spirit of service, and they will show you the way.

scenes.headline: Self-Knowledge Destroys All Sin and Karmic Bondage
visual: As fire turns wood to ash
Knowledge burns away all karma
Even the worst can cross on this raft
scenes.say: Lesson eleven. Self-knowledge destroys all sin and karmic bondage. As a blazing fire turns wood to ash, the fire of knowledge burns away all karma. Even the most sinful person can cross the ocean of wrongdoing on the raft of self-knowledge. No one is beyond it.

scenes.headline: Faith and Sincerity Are Prerequisites for Receiving Knowledge
visual: Faith, sincere practice, control of the senses
Then knowledge reveals itself
Without them it cannot take root
scenes.say: Lesson twelve. Faith and sincerity are prerequisites for receiving knowledge. Knowledge reveals itself, naturally and in time, to the person who has faith, practises sincerely and keeps the senses in check. Without these, it has nowhere to take root.

scenes.headline: Cut Doubt With the Sword of Self-Knowledge, Then Act
visual: Doubt, not difficulty, is the real obstacle
Cut it with the sword of knowledge
Then stand up and act
scenes.say: Lesson thirteen. Cut doubt with the sword of self-knowledge, then act. Krishna's last words here are a command. Doubt, not difficulty, is the real obstacle. Destroy it with knowledge, take up selfless action, and stand up.

scenes.headline: Knowledge that frees the hands
visual: The teaching is ancient, and God renews it
Selfless action binds no one
Knowledge burns karma; doubt must be cut
scenes.say: So, Chapter Four. The teaching is ancient, and God himself renews it whenever it is lost. Selfless action is the deepest kind of stillness, and binds no one. The fire of knowledge burns away all karma. And doubt must be cut, so that we can rise and act. Next, Arjuna asks once more: renunciation or action, which is better?
